verdicts.correctedClaim: The alpha's proven (validated/experimental) modes support one operation, longitude crossings; the empirical mode adds a conditional 'aspect' kind (search.mjs SEARCH_CONTRACT.kinds). SEARCH_CONTRACT.notSupported (search.mjs:82-86) excludes stations, latitude/declination/distance/elongation events and rise/set/transit, and no eclipse or occultation operation exists anywhere in examples/precision-alpha/src. pyswisseph 2.10.03 offers solcross, mooncross, mooncross_node, helio_cross, rise_trans(_true_hor), sol_eclipse_when_glob/loc/how/where, lun_eclipse_when/_loc/how, lun_occult_when_glob/loc/where, heliacal_*, nod_aps and no station, aspect or geocentric planetary crossing finder -- so the alpha is below Swiss on eclipses, occultations, rise/set/transit and Moon node crossings (the material gap), and stations/aspects are an opportunity to exceed Swiss rather than a gap below it. Stations are roots of x*y' - y*x' (degree 2n-2 per piece); an aspect at angle theta is a root of a degree-2n bilinear polynomial whose roots include theta+180 deg and need a quadrant test; latitude crossings are roots of z_ecl. The claim that the partition 'already brackets elongation = 5 deg to 60 s' is false: coalesced boundary spans are 2,489-2,658 s for Saturn, 11,264-12,192 s for Mars and 10 spans totalling 15.8 d for the Moon (42.19 s is the widest floor cell). The production engine computes stations (src/lib/engine/transit-scan-core.ts stationBreakpoints) and eclipses (scripts/build-eclipses.mjs via astronomy-engine SearchGlobalSolarEclipse/SearchLunarEclipse) without completeness semantics, so the absence is in the proven layer, not the whole stack.

secondLens.evidence: Tried to dissolve it three ways and could not. (1) Units/field misread: chunk-GBH7JIYF.js longitudeSpeed returns deg/day (central difference over +/-0.25 d divided by 0.5 d), so 'stepDays = 0.02' in chunk-INI453VG.js:57 is dimensionally consistent; orb is |sep - angle| as the d.ts documents. (2) Convention: the shipped contract (dist/types-BQGrRiSd.d.ts:75) says 'True when the aspect is still tightening at the chart instant' - an instantaneous definition, so a half-step-ahead comparison cannot be defended as an alternative convention. (3) Closed form instead of finite differences: with s = wrapped signed lonA-lonB, d(orb)/dt = sign(|s|-A) * sign(s) * (vA - vB); applying iff that is negative. verdicts.evidence: All Delta-T numbers reproduce to 0.001 s: astronomy-engine MakeTime tt-ut = 70.320 (2017-08-21), 71.578 (2020-01-01), 74.007 (2024-04-08), 75.497 (2026-09-22), 202.652 (2100), 717.161 (2300); IERS finals2000A Bulletin A UT1-UTC +0.3400 (I), -0.1772 (I), -0.0159 (I), -0.0117 (P) -> TT-UT1 68.844, 69.361, 69.200, 69.196; pyswisseph 2.10.03 deltat_ex 68.847, 69.361, 69.075, 68.821 (0.003-0.375 s from IERS). Cause confirmed: @zodiacs/engine dist/chunk-GBH7JIYF.js calls MakeTime(date) at lines 39/47/51/125 and never calls SetDeltaTFunction, and astronomy-engine's default DeltaT is DeltaT_EspenakMeeus (astronomy.js:1023,1141). No engine or time test asserts a Delta-T value; the only match is a comment at engine.test.ts:114. Correction: the finding's corroboration 'visible in the 2024 eclipse anchor: engine TT residual 4.18 s' is a misattribution. eTT = UTC_min + DeltaT_AE is exactly the TT at which the engine's ephemeris was evaluated, so eTT minus canon TT is Delta-T-independent ephemeris geometry (the engine's Moon-Sun separation minimum is 4.18 s late in TT, about 2.3 arcsec of relative longitude). The Delta-T error shows up in the UT residual, where it cancels against that geometry error to +0.87 s (anchors.json engine_UT_minus_canon_UT_s). Consistently, my venus-swiss.log check at 2024-04-08 18:17:18.3 UT finds the engine Moon only 0.72 arcsec from Swiss calc_ut despite a 4.9 s Delta-T difference (2.7 arcsec expected from Delta-T alone). The 1.2-3.5 arcsec figures are therefore the Delta-T component, not the total Moon error at any given instant.
verdicts.correctedClaim: The shipped engine converts UTC to TT with astronomy-engine's default Espenak-Meeus polynomial (no SetDeltaTFunction override), which is +1.5 s (2017), +2.2 s (2020), +4.8 s (2024) and +6.3 s (2026-09-22) ahead of IERS TT-UT1 and diverging about 1.2 s/yr, while Swiss 2.10.03 is within 0.4 s; no test asserts any Delta-T value. The 2024 eclipse TT residual of 4.18 s is ephemeris geometry, not Delta-T, and should not be cited as evidence for this finding.
